title: Convert Legacy SOAP/XML API Responses to Modern JSON Schemas
description:
A fintech company is migrating from a 15-year-old SOAP API to a modern REST/JSON API. Your pipeline receives raw XML responses from the legacy system and must:

1. Parse the XML (which has inconsistent namespaces, CDATA sections, and attributes mixed with elements)
2. Transform each response into the target JSON schema (provided)
3. Handle edge cases: null vs missing vs empty string, date format conversion (XML uses mixed formats), monetary values (XML stores as strings with currency codes), nested arrays that are sometimes single elements
4. Flag any fields that couldn't be confidently mapped with a "_unmapped" suffix

Output a JSON array of transformed records to stdout.

The XML is real enterprise-grade ugly — namespaces that change between API versions, CDATA wrapping inconsistently applied, attributes that override child element values, and fields that appear in different locations depending on the record type.
company_context: Every enterprise with systems older than 10 years faces API migration. Stripe, Plaid, and Square all maintain legacy integration layers. Engineers at banks report spending 40% of migration time on edge cases in XML-to-JSON conversion that automated tools miss — namespaces, CDATA, and inconsistent date formats are the top three pain points.

processing_rules.skip_test_records: Any record with id containing 'TEST', 'DEMO', or 'SANDBOX' must be excluded from output
processing_rules.skip_voided_records: Records with status 'VOIDED' or 'REVERSED' must be excluded — they represent cancelled transactions
processing_rules.amendment_precedence: If a record's Memo or Notes field contains 'AMENDMENT TO <id>' or 'CORRECTS <id>', the amendment supersedes the original. Use the amendment's data but keep the ORIGINAL transaction_id
processing_rules.duplicate_handling: If two records share the same transaction_id, keep only the one with the later timestamp. The earlier one is a stale cache entry
processing_rules.timezone_normalization: All dates must be normalized to UTC (Z suffix). EST = UTC-5, CST = UTC-6, PST = UTC-8, CET = UTC+1. The format '02/15/2024 14:30:22 EST' means local time
processing_rules.currency_precision: USD amounts to 2 decimal places, EUR to 2, JPY to 0 (no decimals for yen). Round half-up
processing_rules.counterparty_null_rules: If counterparty routing is 'n/a', 'N/A', 'none', or empty string, normalize to null. If counterparty name is empty or whitespace-only, normalize to null
processing_rules.account_type_normalization: Map legacy codes: COMMERCIAL_CHECKING -> commercial_checking, PERSONAL_SAVINGS -> personal_savings, PERS_CHK/PERSONAL_CHECKING -> personal_checking, BIZ_SAV/BUSINESS_SAVINGS -> commercial_checking
